newsitem.title: GERMANY: Pan-German Jan inflation edges up 1.8 pct y/y.
newsitem.headline: Pan-German Jan inflation edges up 1.8 pct y/y.

text.p: German consumer price inflation in January, driven by winter price increases, rose 1.8 percent year-on-year, after a 1.4 percent increase the month before, the Federal Statistics Office said on Monday.
January prices across Germany rose 0.5 percent against the previous month's levels. In December, consumer prices edged up 0.3 percent month-on-month.

The final January data also showed west German consumer prices rose slightly faster than preliminary data indicated, as the index increased 1.9 percent year-on-year and 0.5 percent month-on-month. Preliminary figures showed 1.8 and 0.4 percent increases in west Germany.
East German consumer prices for January increased 1.7 percent year-on-year and 0.7 percent month-on-month.
Seasonal factors drove much of the increase as fresh vegetable prices jumped 34.2 percent from December and fuel prices 8.4 percent month-on-month, the Statistics Office said.
Increases in radio and television fees, public transportation fares and telephone rates also contributed to the price rises.
